paragraphs: Lamar Advertising Company is one of the largest outdoor advertising companies in the United States based on number of displays and has operated under the Lamar name since 1902. We manage our business through three operating segments –billboard, logo and transit advertising. We rent space for advertising on billboards, buses, shelters, benches, logo plates and in airport terminals. We offer our customers a fully integrated service, satisfying all aspects of their display requirements from ad copy production to placement and maintenance.
We operate three types of outdoor advertising displays: billboards, logo signs and transit advertising displays.

Billboards. As of December 31, 2025, we owned and operated approximately 159,300 billboard advertising displays in 45 states and Canada. We rent most of our advertising space on two types of billboards: bulletins and posters.
•Bulletins are generally large, illuminated advertising structures that are located on major highways and target vehicular traffic.
•Posters are generally smaller advertising structures that are located on major traffic arteries and city streets and target vehicular and pedestrian traffic.

In addition to traditional billboards, we also rent space on digital billboards, which are generally located on major traffic arteries and city streets. As of December 31, 2025, we owned and operated approximately 5,500 digital billboard advertising displays in 43 states and Canada.
Logo signs. We rent advertising space on logo signs located near highway exits.
•Logo signs generally advertise nearby gas, food, camping, lodging and other attractions.

We are the largest provider of logo signs in the United States, operating 24 of the 28 privatized state logo sign contracts. As of December 31, 2025, we operated over 144,400 logo sign advertising displays in 24 states and the province of Ontario, Canada.

Transit advertising displays. We also rent advertising space on the exterior and interior of public transportation vehicles, in airport terminals, and on transit shelters and benches in over 80 markets. As of December 31, 2025, we operated approximately 40,600 transit advertising displays in 23 states and Canada.
We have operated under the Lamar name since our founding in 1902 and have been publicly traded on NASDAQ under the symbol "LAMR" since 1996.

During 2014, we completed a reorganization in order to qualify as a real estate investment trust (a "REIT") for federal income tax purposes. During 2022, the Company completed a tax reorganization to a specific type of REIT known as an Umbrella Partnership Real Estate Investment Trust ("UPREIT"). The UPREIT structure allows property owners of appreciated properties to contribute property to the operating partnership of the REIT, on a tax-deferred basis, in exchange for a partnership interest in the form of operating partnership units.

In this Annual Report, unless the context otherwise requires, we refer to Lamar Advertising Company and its consolidated subsidiaries (and its predecessor and its consolidated subsidiaries), as applicable, as the "Company", "Lamar Advertising" or "we", and we refer to Lamar Advertising's wholly owned subsidiary Lamar Media Corp. as "Lamar Media."

headings: Risks Related to Our Capital Structure
The Company's substantial debt may adversely affect its business, financial condition and financial results.
The Company may be unable to generate sufficient cash flow to satisfy its significant debt service obligations.

The Company is controlled by significant stockholders who have the power to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to the stockholders for approval and whose interest in the Company may be different than yours.
Our UPREIT structure may result in potential conflicts of interest.
Risks Related to Our Business
The Company could suffer losses due to asset impairment charges for goodwill and other intangible assets.
The Company's logo sign contracts are subject to state award and renewal.
The Company's transit advertising contracts are subject to the Company's ability to obtain and renew favorable contracts with municipalities and airport authorities.
If the Company's contingency plans relating to hurricanes and other natural disasters fail, the resulting losses could hurt the Company's business.
The Company's strategy involves continued investment in its digital platform, and we may fail to realize certain expected benefits of these investments and such investments may become more costly.
Our cash distributions are not guaranteed and may fluctuate.

The Lamar Advertising charter, the Lamar Advertising bylaws and Delaware law may inhibit a takeover that stockholders consider favorable and could also limit the market price of Lamar Advertising stock.
Risks Related to Our Industry
The Company's revenues are sensitive to the state of the economy and the financial markets generally and other external events beyond the Company's control.
The Company faces competition from larger and more diversified outdoor advertisers and other forms of advertising that could hurt its performance.
Additional content-based restrictions on the categories of customers that can advertise on our outdoor advertising structures may be implemented by governmental authorities.
Federal, state and local regulation impact the Company's operations, financial condition and financial results.
Our business and operations could suffer in the event of cybersecurity breaches and we may incur significant legal and financial exposure.
We could be negatively impacted by environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability matters.
Risks Related to Our Status as a REIT
Dividends payable by REITs generally do not qualify for the reduced tax rates on dividend income from non-REIT corporations.
Gain on disposition of assets deemed held for sale in the ordinary course of business is subject to 100% tax.
Failure to make sufficient distributions would jeopardize Lamar Advertising's qualification as a REIT and/or would subject it to U.S. federal income and excise taxes.
Covenants specified in our existing and future debt instruments may limit Lamar Advertising's ability to make required REIT distributions.
Lamar Advertising and its subsidiaries may be required to borrow funds, sell assets, or raise equity to satisfy its REIT distribution requirements or maintain the asset tests.
Complying with REIT requirements may cause Lamar Advertising or its subsidiaries (other than TRSs) to forego otherwise attractive opportunities.
Ownership limitations contained in the Lamar Advertising charter may restrict stockholders from acquiring or transferring certain amounts of shares.
If Lamar Advertising's operating partnership does not qualify as a partnership, its income may be subject to taxation, and Lamar Advertising would no longer qualify as a REIT.
Lamar Advertising may potentially be unable to deduct the full amount of its interest expense.
Legislative changes or other actions affecting REITs could have a negative effect on Lamar Advertising and its subsidiaries.
The ability of the Board of Directors of Lamar Advertising to revoke its REIT election, without stockholder approval, may cause adverse consequences to its stockholders.
We are subject to risks related to our use of Artificial Intelligence.
paragraphs: The Company has borrowed substantially in the past and will continue to borrow in the future. At December 31, 2025, Lamar Advertising Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Lamar Media, had approximately $3.42 billion of total debt outstanding, net of deferred financing costs, consisting of approximately $688.6 million in bank debt outstanding under Lamar Media's senior credit facility, $2.48 billion in various series of senior notes, $249.6 million under the Accounts Receivable Securitization Program and $0.8 million in other seller notes. Despite the level of debt presently outstanding, the terms of the indentures governing Lamar Media's notes and the terms of the senior credit facility and Accounts Receivable Securitization Program allow Lamar Media to incur substantially more debt, including approximately $742.2 million available for borrowing under the revolving credit facility as of December 31, 2025.
The Company's substantial debt and its use of cash flow from operations to make principal and interest payments on its debt may, among other things:

•make it more difficult for the Company to comply with the financial covenants in its senior credit facility and in its Accounts Receivable Securitization Program, which could result in a default and an acceleration of all amounts outstanding under the facility or under the Accounts Receivable Securitization Program;
•limit the cash flow available to fund the Company's working capital, capital expenditures, acquisitions or other general corporate requirements;
•limit the Company's ability to obtain additional financing to fund future dividend distributions, working capital, capital expenditures or other general corporate requirements;
•place the Company at a competitive disadvantage relative to those of its competitors that have less debt;

The following is a discussion of the consolidated financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024. This discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements of the Company and the related notes.
Discussion of our results of operations for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 can be found in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The Company's net revenues are derived primarily from the rental of advertising space on outdoor advertising displays owned and operated by the Company. We manage our business through three operating segments – billboard, logo and transit advertising. Revenue growth is based on many factors that include the Company's ability to increase occupancy of its existing advertising displays; raise advertising rates; and acquire new advertising displays and its operating results are therefore affected by general economic conditions, as well as trends in the advertising industry. Advertising spending is particularly sensitive to changes in general economic conditions, which affect the rates the Company is able to charge for advertising on its displays and its ability to maximize advertising sales or occupancy on its displays.

Historically, the Company has made strategic acquisitions of outdoor advertising assets to increase the number of outdoor advertising displays it operates in existing and new markets. The Company continues to evaluate and pursue strategic acquisition opportunities as they arise. The Company has financed its historical acquisitions and intends to finance any future acquisition activity from available cash, borrowings under the senior credit facility and the Accounts Receivable Securitization Program or through the issuance of debt or equity securities. See "Liquidity and Capital Resources- Sources of Cash," for more information.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company completed multiple acquisitions for a total cash purchase price of approximately $191.1 million. See "Uses of Cash-Acquisitions," for more information. Additionally, Lamar Advertising Limited Partnership ("Lamar LP"), the subsidiary operating partnership of the Company and Lamar Media, acquired Verde Outdoor at a value of $147.6 million through the issuance of 1,187,500 Common Units of Lamar LP. The Common Units were issued to the owners of Verde Outdoor as the consideration in connection with the acquisition, whereby the assets of Verde Outdoor were contributed to Lamar LP. The Verde Outdoor assets include more than 1,500 billboard faces across ten states.

The Company's business requires expenditures for maintenance and capitalized costs associated with the construction of new billboard displays, the entrance into and renewal of logo sign and transit contracts, and the purchase of real estate and operating equipment. We expect our 2026 capital expenditures to be approximately $186 million. NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES

Our management reviews our performance by focusing on several key performance indicators not prepared in conformity with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States ("GAAP"). We believe these non-GAAP performance indicators are meaningful supplemental measures of our operating performance and should not be considered in isolation of, or as a substitute for, their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures.

Included in our analysis of our results of operations are discussions regarding earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("adjusted EBITDA"), Funds From Operations ("FFO"), as defined by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts, Adjusted Funds From Operations ("AFFO") and acquisition-adjusted net revenues.

We define adjusted EBITDA as net income before income tax expense (benefit), interest expense (income), equity in (earnings) loss of investee, loss (gain) on extinguishment of debt and investments, stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, loss (gain) on disposition of assets and investments, transaction expenses and capitalized contract fulfillment costs, net. Our management uses this measure internally to evaluate the performance of our business as a whole and our individual business segments.

FFO is defined as net income before (gain) loss from the sale or disposal of real estate assets and investments, net of tax, and real estate related depreciation and amortization and including adjustments to eliminate unconsolidated affiliates and non-controlling interest.

paragraphs: Lamar Advertising Company 是美國最大的戶外廣告公司之一，根據顯示螢幕數量來計算，自 1902 年以來一直以 Lamar 名義營運。我們透過三個營運分部來管理業務 – 戶外廣告、標誌廣告與交通廣告。我們出租廣告空間於路牌、公車、站臺、長椅、標誌板與機場大廳。我們為客戶提供完整的整合服務，滿足其所有顯示需求，從廣告文案製作到放置與維護。
我們經營三種類型的戶外廣告顯示螢幕：路牌、標誌板與交通廣告顯示螢幕。
路牌。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有並營運約 159,300 個路牌廣告顯示螢幕，分佈於 45 個州與加拿大。我們出租大多數廣告空間於兩種類型的路牌：公告板與海報。
•公告板通常是大型、發光的廣告結構，位於主要高速公路，針對車輛流量。
•海報通常是較小的廣告結構，位於主要交通幹道與城市街道，針對車輛與行人流量。
除了傳統的路牌外，我們也出租空間於數位路牌，這些數位路牌通常位於主要交通幹道與城市街道。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有並營運約 5,500 個數位路牌廣告顯示螢幕，分佈於 43 個州與加拿大。
標誌板。我們出租廣告空間於位於高速公路出口附近的標誌板。
•標誌板通常用來宣傳附近的加油站、餐飲、露營、住宿及其他景點。
本公司為美國最大的標誌看板供應商，經營28個私有化州政府標誌看板契約中的24個。截至2025年12月31日，本公司在24個州及加拿大安大略省運作逾144,400個標誌看板廣告展示。
交通廣告展示。本公司亦出租公共運輸車輛的內外空間、機場大廳，以及交通站點與長椅等超過80個市場的廣告空間。截至2025年12月31日，本公司在23個州及加拿大運作約40,600個交通廣告展示。
本公司自1902年成立以來一直以Lamar為名運作，並自1996年起在NASDAQ以符號"LAMR"公開上市交易。

2014年，本公司完成一項重組，以符合美國聯邦所得稅法規的不動產投資信託（"REIT"）資格。2022年，本公司完成一項稅務重組，轉型為一種特定類型的REIT，稱為"Umbrella Partnership Real Estate Investment Trust（"UPREIT"）"。UPREIT結構允許擁有增值不動產的業主，以延稅方式將其不動產投入REIT的運作合夥企業，並換取合夥企業單位形式的運作合夥單位。
在本年度報告中，除非上下文另有說明，否則我們指稱Lamar Advertising Company及其合併子公司（及其前身及其合併子公司），如適用，為"本公司"、"Lamar Advertising"或"我們"，我們亦指稱Lamar Advertising的 wholly owned subsidiary Lamar Media Corp. 為"Lamar Media."

以下為本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度之合併財務狀況與營運成果之討論。此討論應與本公司之合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。
本公司 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日結算年度之營運成果討論，請參閱本公司 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度之 10-K 年度報告第 II 部分，第 7 項。

本公司之淨營收主要來自於本公司所有並營運之戶外廣告顯示裝置之廣告空間租賃。本公司透過三個營運分部來管理業務 – 戶外廣告、標誌廣告與交通廣告。營收成長取決於許多因素，包括本公司提升現有廣告顯示裝置使用率之能力、提高廣告費用率以及取得新廣告顯示裝置，因此本公司營運成果受總體經濟狀況以及廣告產業趨勢影響。廣告支出尤其對總體經濟狀況的變化敏感，這會影響本公司在顯示裝置上所能收取的廣告費用率，以及本公司最大化廣告銷售或使用率之能力。
歷來，本公司已透過戰略性收購戶外廣告資產，以增加其在現有及新市場所營運之戶外廣告顯示裝置數量。本公司持續評估並追求出現的戰略性收購機會。本公司已透過現金、高階信貸融資及應收帳款證券化計畫來資金融資其歷來收購活動，並有意透過發行債務或股權證券來資金融資任何未來收購活動。有關更多資訊，請參閱 "流動性與資本資源-現金來源"。

於 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度，本公司完成多項收購，總現金購買價格約為 1.911 億美元。有關更多資訊，請參閱 "現金運用-收購"。此外，本公司之子公司營運合夥企業 "Lamar LP"（"Lamar LP"）與 Lamar Media 收購 Verde Outdoor，價值為 1.476 億美元，透過發行 1,187,500 張 Lamar LP 普通單位（Common Units of Lamar LP）完成。這些普通單位發行給 Verde Outdoor 之所有者作為收購對價， whereby Verde Outdoor 之資產已轉讓至 Lamar LP。Verde Outdoor 之資產包括超過 1,500 個廣告牌面，分佈於十個州。
本公司業務需要支出用於維護及資本支出，與新戶外廣告顯示裝置之建設、標誌廣告與交通合約之進入與續約，以及購買不動產與營運設備相關。以下表格呈現過去兩年之資本支出分解：

我們的管理階層透過關注幾個關鍵績效指標來評估我們的表現，這些指標並未依照美國通用會計原則（"GAAP"）編製。我們認為這些非 GAAP 表現指標是我們營運表現有意義的補充措施，不應與其最直接可比的 GAAP 財務指標孤立或作為替代。
我們在分析營運結果時，包含有關營運前利息、稅項、折舊及攤銷（"調整後 EBITDA"）、資金從營運（"FFO"），如國家不動產投資信託協會所定義，調整後資金從營運（"AFFO"）及取得調整後淨收入的討論。
我們將調整後 EBITDA 定義為淨收入扣除所得稅費用（收益）、利息費用（收入）、投資收益（損失）、債務減免損益及投資、股票基於報酬、折舊及攤銷、資產及投資處置損益、交易費用及資本化契約履行成本，淨額。我們的管理階層使用此指標內部評估我們整體業務及各個業務分部的表現。
FFO 被定義為淨收入扣除出售或處置不動產資產及投資的損益（淨額），以及與不動產相關的折舊及攤銷，並包含調整以消除未合併附屬公司及非控制性權益。

headings: 與本公司資本結構相關的風險
本公司龐大的債務可能對其業務、財務狀況及財務結果產生不利影響。
本公司可能無法產生足夠的現金流量以償還其重大債務償還義務。
本公司由具重大股權的股東控制，這些股東有權決定提交股東批准的所有事項結果，且其對本公司的利益可能與您的利益不同。
本公司的UPREIT結構可能導致潛在的利益衝突。
與本公司業務相關的風險
本公司可能因商譽及其他無形資產的減損費用而遭受損失。
本公司之商標招牌合約受州政府獎勵及續約條款所限制。
本公司之轉運廣告契約取決於本公司能否取得並續約有利之與市轄政府及機場主管機關之契約。
若本公司針對颶風及其他天然災害之應變計畫失敗，所導致之損失可能影響本公司之營運。
本公司策略包含持續投資於其數位平台，我們可能無法實現某些預期之投資效益，且這些投資可能變得更加昂貴。
本公司現金分紅並無保證，可能有所波動。
拉馬廣告公司章程、拉馬廣告公司規章及特拉華州法律可能抑制股東認為有利之併購，同時也可能限制拉馬廣告股票之市場價格。
與我們產業相關之風險
本公司之營業收入對總體經濟及財務市場之狀態及其他超出本公司控制之外部事件具有高度敏感性。
本公司面臨來自較大且更具多元性之戶外廣告商及其他形式廣告之競爭，可能影響其營運表現。
政府機關可能針對可在本公司戶外廣告結構上刊登廣告之客戶類別，實施更多基於內容的限制。
聯邦、州及地方的法規會影響本公司的營運、財務狀況及財務成果。
若發生網路安全事件，本公司營運與業務可能受影響，且本公司可能面臨重大法律與財務風險。
本公司可能因環境、社會及治理（ESG）及永續議題而受到負面影響。
與本公司作為REIT地位相關之風險
REIT所支付之股息，通常無法適用對非REIT公司股息收入之減稅率。
在正常營運過程中，將資產處分所產生之獲利，若被視為持有待售，則需課徵100%稅額。
若未能足夠發放股息，將危及Lamar Advertising作為REIT之資格，且可能使其面臨美國聯邦所得稅及調節稅
本公司現有及未來債務契約中所規定的約束條款，可能限制 Lamar Advertising 進行必要的 REIT 分紅能力。
Lamar Advertising 及其子公司可能需要借款、出售資產或發行股權，以符合其 REIT 分紅要求或維持資產測試標準。
符合 REIT 要求可能導致 Lamar Advertising 或其子公司（除 TRSs 以外）放棄其他否則具有吸引力的機會。
Lamar Advertising 公司章程中所含的股東持股限制，可能限制股東取得或轉讓特定數量的股份。
若 Lamar Advertising 的營運合夥企業無法符合合夥企業的標準，其所得可能需課稅，而 Lamar Advertising 將無法繼續符合 REIT 的條件。
Lamar Advertising 有可能無法完全扣除其利息支出。
影響 REIT 的立法變更或其他行動，可能對 Lamar Advertising 及其子公司產生負面影響。
Lamar Advertising 董事會無需股東批准即可撤銷其 REIT 選擇權，可能對其股東產生不利後果。

paragraphs: 本公司過去曾大量舉債，並將持續在未來舉債。至2025年12月31日，Lamar Advertising Company的 wholly owned subsidiary，Lamar Media，總計未償還債務約為34.2億美元，扣除延後融資費用後，包含約68.86億美元的銀行貸款，係根據Lamar Media的高階信用融資計畫所發行，約248億美元的各系列高階債券，約24.96億美元根據帳款資通融資計畫，以及約0.8萬美元的其他賣方貸款。儘管目前未償還債務水準，根據Lamar Media債券的抵押契約條款以及高階信用融資計畫與帳款資通融資計畫的條款，Lamar Media仍可償還 substantially more 債務，包括截至2025年12月31日，根據循環信用融資計畫可借款約74.22億美元。
本公司大量債務以及使用營運現金流來償還債務的本金與利息，可能會導致以下情況：
•使本公司更難以符合高階信用融資計畫與帳款資通融資計畫中的財務契約條款，這可能會導致違約並加速所有未償還金額的償還；
•限制本公司可用以支應營運資金、資本支出、收購或其他一般企業需求的現金流；
•限制本公司取得額外融資以支應未來股息發放、營運資金、資本支出或其他一般企業需求的能力；
•使本公司相較於債務較少的競爭對手處於競爭劣勢；
